concerns: Measurement feasibility: Immuno‑capture + particle‑count workflows recommended by MISEV require validation for low‑biomass lavage/CSF samples; current large‑animal negative biodistribution (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution) implies high false‑negative risk unless assay sensitivity/labeling and sampling windows are proven.

Manufacturability / process sensitivity: Preserving a membrane‑protected, capture‑positive fraction through scalable operations (TFF/SEC/centrifugation, concentration, formulation) is likely sensitive to shear, detergents, buffers and requires process maps to avoid activity loss (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Scale‑up risk: Source‑cell scale (even if immortalized clones show efficacy in rodents, ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi) may not yield consistent capture‑positive yields or same cargo distributions at manufacturing scale; fractionation yields and particle:protein ratios may change, impacting the proposed attribute.

Lot comparability: Demonstrating the proposed qualitative potency gate (capture‑positive + detergent‑sensitive) across independent lots will require robust in‑process controls and release assays — currently unproven for low‑biomass in vivo exposure endpoints.

Stability: Membrane integrity (required for the attribute) is inherently labile; storage, freeze‑thaw, and formulation conditions may abolish the attribute and need formal stability data linking integrity to functional readout.

Translational risk: Rodent intranasal efficacy (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi) supports mechanism plausibility but non‑human‑primate negative biodistribution (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution) raises substantial risk that intranasal delivery of intact EVs to relevant CNS compartments will not translate, undermining the relevance of an EV‑centric potency attribute.
conclusion: Not supported by available evidence as a de-risked, manufacturing-ready claim. Rodent efficacy and MISEV2023 recommend orthogonal EV characterization and make the hypothesis plausible, but non-human-primate intranasal biodistribution that failed to detect EV brain/CSF exposure and multiple analytical gaps mean this candidate potency attribute carries high process, measurement, scale-up, and translation risk without additional bridging data.
evidence_gap: Critical gaps: validated orthogonal intact‑EV assays sensitive in low‑biomass matrices (nasal lavage, CSF, olfactory mucosa) and demonstration of in vivo intact‑EV exposure in a large‑animal model after intranasal dosing; data showing preservation of membrane integrity and bioactivity through scalable fractionation/formulation and stability over relevant storage/handling; lot‑to‑lot reproducibility of the capture‑positive signature correlated with function across independent manufacturing runs.
